biography.background:
Darth Pleïa est un Guerrier Infernis de l'école "Call of the Brave". Elle est brave : elle n'a peur de personne, mais tout le monde a peur d'elle dès qu'elle commence à faire tournoyer son épée laser.

Comment jouer Darth Pleïa ?

  • Vous n'avez peur de rien, lorsque vous faites un jet avec Fear, vous avez sans doute une solution.

  • Vous êtes sans pitié, vos adversaires feraient mieux de ne pas fuir s'ils ne veulent pas se faire attaquer dans le dos !

  • Utilisez @UUID[Compendium.daggerheart.subclasses.qqb5acyUSl1sCpWW]{Battle Ritual} pour méditer quelques secondes avant un conbat important afin de récupérer vos ressources !

  • Votre technique est impréssionante, lorsque vous faites des dégâts, relancez tous les dés qui n'ont qu'un résultat de 1 ou 2 !

system.description:
If an adversary within Melee range attempts to leave that range, make a reaction roll using a trait of your choice against their Difficulty. Choose one effect on a success, or two if you critically succeed:

  • They can't move from where they are.

  • You deal damage to them equal to your primary weapon's damage.

  • You move with them.
You ignore burden when equipping weapons. When you deal physical damage, you gain a bonus to your damage roll equal to your level.

system.description: Becoming a warrior requires years, often a lifetime, of training and dedication to the mastery of weapons and violence. While many who seek to fight hone only their strength, warriors understand the importance of an agile body and mind, making them some of the most sought-after fighters across the realms. Frequently, warriors find employment within an army, a band of mercenaries, or even a royal guard, but their potential is wasted in any position where they cannot continue to improve and expand their skills. Warriors are known to have a favored weapon; to come between them and their blade would be a grievous mistake.

system.description: When you roll with Fear, you can mark 2 Stress to change it into a roll with Hope instead.
Once per Long Rest, when you would gain Fear on an Action Roll, you may instead reroll your Hope die and keep the new result.

Once per long rest, before you attempt something incredibly dangerous or face off against a foe who clearly outmatches you, describe what ritual you perform or preparations you make. When you do, clear 2 Stress and gain 2 Hope.
You are vigilant in the face of mounting danger. While you have 2 or fewer Hit Points unmarked, you can roll a d20 as your Hope Die.
When you fail a roll with Fear, you gain a Hope.

Your unwavering bravery is a rallying point for your allies. You can initiate a Tag Team Roll one additional time per session. Additionally, when an ally initiates a Tag Team Roll with you, they only need to spend 2 Hope to do so.

system.description: Infernis are humanoids who possess sharp canine teeth, pointed ears, and horns. They are the descendants of demons from the Circles Below.

Being part of a faithborne community means your society was united by a shared spiritual tradition, whether devoted to ancient cosmic entities, the Resonance itself, or a philosophical order. Faith shapes not only your beliefs, but how you approach hardship and hope.

Faithborne are often compassionate, devoted, humble, insightful, serene, and steadfast.
Play the Call of the Brave if you want to use the might of your enemies to fuel your own power.
